history.dynasty: Ancient Mithila tradition; no documented dynastic founder
history.period: Ancient Shakta pitha; temple antiquity in local legend
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV says Madhubani, but the temple is at Uchhaith (also spelled Uchchaith/Uchaitha) village in Benipatti block, ~22 km from Madhubani town — town and district fields corrected accordingly. Ancient Shakta pitha of Mithila dedicated to the headless goddess (Chhinnamastika-like form), locally called Banadevi; the shrine's blog describes it as 'मां काली का सिद्धपीठ' (siddhapeetha of Maa Kali). Legend: sages Kapila, Kanada, Gautam and others passed through Uchhaith on their journeys to the Himalayas or Janakpur; the Sanskrit poet Kalidasa is said to have received blessings from Bhagwati here, and local belief holds children initiated into the alphabet with this soil become scholars. Opening hours conflict: travelsetu 5:00 AM–9:00 PM vs place-listing 6:00 AM–8:00 PM — marked verify. Coordinates from Wikipedia (26.4639763, 85.8781971).

name: Uchhaith Bhagwati Temple
town_description: Uchhaith is a small historic village in Benipatti block of Madhubani district, in the Mithila region of Bihar — a land of Madhubani painting, ancient Vedic scholarship, and Shakta pilgrimage tradition on the western bank of the Thumne river.
